name: Reality Rulebook
tagline: Everyday things, slowed down until the physics shows.
promise: One everyday event, slowed down and measured on screen until the rule behind it shows. Every number is sourced or computed, and every simplification wears a badge.

identity.look: Daylight lab: a warm-paper backdrop curve (the cyc) ruled like a measuring board and lit like a high-speed photo studio. The only light-background channel. Display type is Archivo at weight 800, width 125.
identity.lighting: Soft key from above front-left, hemisphere fill, cool rim from behind. No shadow maps today. Bloom threshold 2.5 or more and prop albedo 0.7 or below, so the cyc lands on its token after ACES.
identity.camera: Locked 'measure view', square to the grid, long lens (portrait field of view 30 to 36 degrees), deep focus. Slider drifts of 2 to 5 cm a second. One 60 to 90 degree turn per episode, landing on a starred word. Macro pushes into contact moments.
identity.materials: Props built from primitives with MeshStandardMaterial. The cyc is an unlit shader fed ACES-inverse values (set/aces.js). Strobe ghosts are opaque and tinted toward the cyc. No transmission: set/straw.js draws glass with a lit, nearly clear standard material.
signatureDevices: Strobe ladder: ghost copies stamped at equal time steps on the ruled backdrop
Spine readout (one live number from hook to end)
Honesty badges in mono: 'slowed xN', 'air ignored', 'illustration', 'model'
A 'measure it' beat with mono readouts
Title card 'the drop': the title falls onto a ruler line and bounces twice
Yellow marker band behind the word being spoken

s3.summary: One daylight kitchen with a window onto a backyard: one second of everyday life, slowed further and further. The slow-motion factor counter is the only text besides the captions.
s3.notes: Source: lf01/script.md and lf01/build.py on the channel branch. A 960x540 16:9 draft is rendered; parts ep13 to ep20 are compiled, not rendered. Title: lf01/script.md on the channel branch now carries 'How Much Would You Slow Time to Watch Light Move?' (commit 83d77da2, 11 Nov 2026), while lf01/packaging.json still names the earlier winner 'Slow Down One Second Until Light Stands Still', which overstates (claim c1 says not literally still). The owner's choice between them is not on record in the repo. A physicist signs off before it posts. No owner approval of a still is on record.

voice.tone: Crisp and curious, like slowing a moment down on purpose so a friend can see it.

sound.music: Preset restframe-bench (kits/cinema/studio/vibes/restframe-bench.json): G mixolydian at 112.5 BPM, so a 16th note is exactly 4 frames; staccato blips over low pads.
sound.foley: Hard and close: knocks, ticks, shutters. Signature: knocks D6, B5, G5 at 0, +12 and +20 frames (a ball bouncing to rest).
rules: Delivered AAC: integrated loudness -15 to -13 LUFS, true peak at most -1 dBTP, mono-safe (kits/cinema/film/qa.py).
Sound transients land within one frame of their picture event (kits/cinema/studio/qa.py).
The strobe never flashes: fewer than 3 bright events a second.

short.notes: Seasons 1 and 2. Native 1080x1920 render; the -9x16-youtube.mp4 file is a 1440x2560 Lanczos upscale, labelled '1440 upscale'. 150 to 180 words (kits/cinema/script/lint.py).

part.notes: Season 3 on: one of the long film's 8 chapters, cut from the film's own 9:16 render (never a crop of the 16:9). Opens with its own 2 s hook line, ends on its cliffhanger, then 'Part N of 8. Full video on YouTube.' Part 8 stops before the payoff.

long.notes: Season 3 on: one continuous 16:9 film. Delivery master that Prism imports: compilations/<name>/<name>-16x9.mp4 at 2560x1440. kits/cinema/film/render.mjs draws the film at 1920x1080; no tool writes the 2560x1440 file yet for one continuous film (Roadmap 2.2). Once it is built by upscale, label it '2560x1440 upscale of a 1080 render', never native 1440p. Seasons 1 and 2 were joined from episodes by kits/cinema/film/compilation.mjs: a 2560x1440 frame with cards drawn at that size and each episode's 1080x1920 master scaled down to 810x1440 (label: '2560x1440 upload; episode picture 810x1440 from the 1080x1920 master'). Runs 8:30 to 9:30, never by padding.

packaging.dna: Physics that looks impossible. A daylight lab or an everyday room, one frozen moment (a splash crown, a bullet's shock cone, a light front), strobe ghost stamps. Clean and exact. A hand or figure caught mid-action at the key frozen moment.

rules: Every factual sentence carries a claims.json tag. A claim is OK only after a person opens the source; anything checked from a search excerpt stays OPEN.
AI voice af_bella at speed 0.85 (kits/cinema/voice/tts.py; ep12/vo/lines.json). Synthetic narration is labelled as AI on every film and post.
Every simplification is badged on screen.
Hook: a question spoken and captioned by 2.0 s.
Reading grade at most 7 and no sentence over 22 words (channel gate, review/clarity-review.md; the shared gate is grade 8).
One 'measure it' beat per episode (kits/cinema/script/lint.py --segment measure).
Cobalt #1F3BD1 is force and the title's accent word on screen. #2F5BFF is the packaging and Prism accent only.
The yellow marker is only the band behind the spoken word.
An opacity of 1/3 keeps about 1/11 of the contrast after ACES: set translucent overlays with set/aces.js screenAlpha.
A physicist signs off each script before it posts (channel bible.md; the reviewing physicist's name is a TODO in every handoff until the owner names one).
One Chromium render job per machine.
never: Never present a render as a photo or a measurement: mark it 'Illustration' or 'Model'.
No Lumevina, Los Güeros or Claude coral colours; no indigo or teal (One More Orbit's).
No more than 3 flashes a second.
No title or thumbnail that claims more than the script.
No exclamation marks, hype words or 'like and subscribe' in the script; the like/follow line comes from films/channels/CTA.md.
Never claim a technique, resolution or metric the engine did not deliver (films/channels/studio/README.md, 'Maximum-fidelity standard').
Nothing posts without the owner; publishing is manual.
